newsitem.title: ABU DHABI: Britain's GEC announces UAE offset project.
newsitem.headline: Britain's GEC announces UAE offset project.

text.p: Britain's GEC-Marconi said on Monday it was setting up a furniture manufacturing firm in the United Arab Emirates as part of its commitments under the UAE's offset programme.

"As part of the offset programme in the UAE, GEC-Marconi has entered into an agreement with a prestigious U.K. company -- J C Maclean -- to set up, with an Abu Dhabi partner, a factory making high quality furniture and interior contracting for palaces, hotels, villas and public buildings," a company statement said.
The statement said at least 50 percent of the factory output would be exported to Europe and the Far East.
No details about the local partner or capital were given.
The company said other projects in the pipeline under the offset programme included the formation of a local company which would charter ships to a UAE ship operator.

Projects also included a joint venture which would provide geological and topographical information to evaluate natural resources -- oil, gas and water -- urban planning and pipeline monitoring by using data from satellites.
The statement did not name the project partners or give details on capital.
GEC-Marconi said earlier on Monday that it would announce up to three offset projects in the UAE during an international arms show in Abu Dhabi this week.
GEC, the defence firm of Britain's General Electric Co, has long-standing ties with Abu Dhabi.
International arms manufacturers supplying the UAE are required to invest a portion of a deal's worth in profitable ventures with a UAE partner under the terms of the offset scheme.
